title: MS Windows Print Spooler Remote Code Execution (PrintNightmare)
description: The Windows Print Spooler service allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges.
recommended_fix: Apply the security update referenced in Microsoft KB5004945 or disable the Print Spooler service on servers that do not require printing.

kev.vulnerability_name: Microsoft Windows Print Spooler Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

title: MS17-010: SMBv1 Remote Code Execution (EternalBlue)
description: The SMBv1 server on the remote host has multiple remote code execution vulnerabilities.
recommended_fix: Apply the MS17-010 patch and/or disable SMBv1 entirely; use SMBv2/v3 instead.

kev.vulnerability_name: Microsoft SMBv1 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

title: Windows MSHTML Platform Security Feature Bypass
description: A security feature bypass exists in the Windows MSHTML platform.
recommended_fix: Install the applicable Windows Update to address CVE-2024-30040.

kev.vulnerability_name: Microsoft Windows MSHTML Platform Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

title: Sudo Heap-Based Buffer Overflow (Baron Samedit)
description: A heap-based buffer overflow in sudo before 1.9.5p2 allows local privilege escalation to root.
recommended_fix: Upgrade sudo to version 1.9.5p2 or later via the distribution package manager.

kev.vulnerability_name: Sudo Heap-Based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

title: OpenSSL Infinite Loop Denial of Service (BN_mod_sqrt)
description: OpenSSL's BN_mod_sqrt() function can be made to loop forever with a malicious certificate, causing a denial of service.
recommended_fix: Upgrade OpenSSL to the patched version provided by the distribution's package manager.

title: Cisco IOS XE Web UI Privilege Escalation
description: A vulnerability in the web UI feature of Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an unauthenticated attacker to create an account with privilege level 15 access.
recommended_fix: Disable the HTTP/HTTPS server feature on internet-facing devices or apply the vendor-provided fix per Cisco's advisory.

kev.vulnerability_name: Cisco IOS XE Web UI Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

title: Device Exposes Telnet Service
description: Device has an open Telnet (port 23) service, which transmits credentials in cleartext and is disabled-by-default on hardened builds.
recommended_fix: Disable Telnet and use the device's encrypted management protocol (SSH/HTTPS) instead.

title: Unauthenticated Access to Management Interface
description: The device's web management interface is reachable without authentication, allowing configuration changes by any network-adjacent host.
recommended_fix: Enable authentication on the management interface and restrict access to an OT management VLAN.

title: Outdated OS Version
description: Device is running an iOS version 3 major releases behind current, missing several security patches.
recommended_fix: Prompt user / enforce MDM compliance policy to update iOS to the current release.

title: Internet-facing RDP discovered on Windows bastion host
description: Weekly external attack-surface sweep found TCP/3389 (RDP) reachable from the internet, outside the approved jump-host allowlist. RDP exposure is a top initial-access vector for ransomware affiliates.
recommended_fix: Restrict RDP to the VPN/jump-host network range via host firewall/NSG rule, and enforce NLA + MFA for any remaining external RDP access.

title: OpenSSH regression allows authentication bypass under non-default config
description: Vendor advisory flags a regression in OpenSSH server affecting hosts with a specific PAM configuration, potentially allowing authentication to be bypassed. Confirmed present on one internal Linux host during config audit.
recommended_fix: Upgrade OpenSSH to the vendor-patched version immediately; this host handles internal authentication traffic.

title: Apache Log4j2 Remote Code Execution (Log4Shell)
description: The order-processing application bundles a vulnerable version of Apache Log4j2. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger remote code execution by causing the application to log a crafted string (JNDI lookup injection).
recommended_fix: Upgrade the bundled Log4j2 library to 2.17.1 or later; do not rely on mitigations like removing JndiLookup.class as a permanent fix.

kev.vulnerability_name: Apache Log4j2 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

title: SSL Certificate Expiry
description: The SSL certificate for this service expires within 30 days. An expired certificate will cause browsers to show trust warnings and may break automated clients that validate certificate expiry.
recommended_fix: Renew and replace the SSL certificate before its expiration date via your CA or ACME automation.

title: Deprecated TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 Protocol Detected
description: The remote service accepts connections encrypted using TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1, both deprecated protocols with known cryptographic weaknesses.
recommended_fix: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 in the web server's TLS configuration; support TLSv1.2 or later only.

title: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect Command Injection
description: A command injection vulnerability in the GlobalProtect gateway/portal feature allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges by creating a crafted file on the system.
recommended_fix: Apply the PAN-OS hotfix referenced in Palo Alto Networks advisory PAN-SA-2024-0010, or disable GlobalProtect gateway/portal telemetry as an interim mitigation if the hotfix cannot be applied immediately.

kev.vulnerability_name: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Command Injection Vulnerability

title: OpenSSL and SSLeay allow remote attackers to reuse SSL sessions and bypass access controls.
description: OpenSSL and SSLeay allow remote attackers to reuse SSL sessions and bypass access controls.
recommended_fix: See vendor advisory for CVE-1999-0428 and apply the corresponding patch/update.

description: OpenSSL 0.9.4 and OpenSSH for FreeBSD do not properly check for the existence of the /dev/random or /dev/urandom devices, which are absent on FreeBSD Alpha systems, which causes them to produce weak keys which may be more easily broken.
recommended_fix: See vendor advisory for CVE-2000-0535 and apply the corresponding patch/update.

description: The Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG) in SSLeay and OpenSSL before 0.9.6b allows attackers to use the output of small PRNG requests to determine the internal state information, which could be used by attackers to predict future pseudo-random numbers.
recommended_fix: See vendor advisory for CVE-2001-1141 and apply the corresponding patch/update.

description: ssl3_get_record in s3_pkt.c for OpenSSL before 0.9.7a and 0.9.6 before 0.9.6i does not perform a MAC computation if an incorrect block cipher padding is used, which causes an information leak (timing discrepancy) that may make it easier to launch cryptographic attacks that rely on distinguishing between padding and MAC verification errors, possibly leading to extraction of the original…

description: The SSL and TLS components for OpenSSL 0.9.6i and earlier, 0.9.7, and 0.9.7a allow remote attackers to perform an unauthorized RSA private key operation via a modified Bleichenbacher attack that uses a large number of SSL or TLS connections using PKCS #1 v1.5 padding that cause OpenSSL to leak information regarding the relationship between ciphertext and the associated plaintext, aka the…

title: OpenSSL does not use RSA blinding by default, which allows local and remote attackers to obtain the server's private…
description: OpenSSL does not use RSA blinding by default, which allows local and remote attackers to obtain the server's private key by determining factors using timing differences on (1) the number of extra reductions during Montgomery reduction, and (2) the use of different integer multiplication algorithms ("Karatsuba" and normal).

description: OpenSSL 0.9.6k allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash via large recursion) via malformed ASN.1 sequences.

title: Weak Password Policy Allows Trivial Brute Force (CWE-521)
description: The login form accepts short, low-complexity passwords with no rate limiting, making credential-stuffing/brute-force attacks practical.
recommended_fix: Enforce a minimum password complexity policy and add rate limiting/account lockout after repeated failed attempts.

title: Missing HTTP Security Headers (CWE-693)
description: The application does not send X-Frame-Options/Content-Security-Policy headers, leaving it vulnerable to clickjacking and reducing defense-in-depth against XSS.
recommended_fix: Add X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and a baseline Content-Security-Policy.

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) (CWE-352)
description: A state-changing request has no anti-CSRF token and is accepted with only a session cookie, allowing a forged cross-site request to perform the action on a victim's behalf.
recommended_fix: Require a per-session anti-CSRF token on all state-changing requests and set the session cookie's SameSite attribute to Strict or Lax.

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (CWE-79)
description: User-submitted content is persisted and rendered to other users without sanitization, allowing a stored payload to execute in any visitor's session.
recommended_fix: Sanitize/encode user content on output (not just input) and use a CSP that blocks inline script execution.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (CWE-79)
description: User-controlled input from a query parameter is reflected into the HTML response without output encoding, allowing arbitrary script execution in a victim's browser.
recommended_fix: Apply context-aware output encoding at every reflection point and adopt a strict Content-Security-Policy as defense in depth.

title: Session Cookie Missing 'Secure' Attribute (CWE-614)
description: The session cookie is not marked Secure, allowing it to be transmitted over an unencrypted HTTP connection if one is ever made.
recommended_fix: Set the Secure attribute on all session/authentication cookies.

title: Open Redirect (CWE-601)
description: A redirect parameter accepts an arbitrary external URL without validation, enabling phishing links that appear to originate from a trusted domain.
recommended_fix: Validate redirect targets against an allowlist of relative paths or known internal hosts only.

title: Hardcoded API Key in Client-Side JavaScript (CWE-798)
description: A third-party API key is embedded directly in a client-side JavaScript bundle, visible to anyone who views the page source.
recommended_fix: Move the API call behind a server-side proxy that holds the credential, or use a public/restricted key scoped for client-side use.

title: Weak Password Policy Allows Trivial Brute Force (CWE-521)
description: The login form accepts short, low-complexity passwords with no rate limiting, making credential-stuffing/brute-force attacks practical.
recommended_fix: Enforce a minimum password complexity policy and add rate limiting/account lockout after repeated failed attempts.

title: Verbose Error Message Discloses Stack Trace (CWE-209)
description: An unhandled exception returns a full stack trace and internal file paths to the client, disclosing implementation details useful for further attack.
recommended_fix: Return generic error responses to clients and log detailed stack traces server-side only.

title: Unrestricted File Upload (CWE-434)
description: The file upload feature does not validate file type/content, allowing a script file to be uploaded and potentially executed by the web server.
recommended_fix: Validate uploaded file content (not just extension), store uploads outside the web root, and disable script execution in the upload directory.

title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection (CWE-611)
description: The XML parser resolves external entities in user-supplied XML, allowing local file disclosure or SSRF via a crafted DOCTYPE declaration.
recommended_fix: Disable external entity resolution and DTD processing in the XML parser configuration.

title: HTTP Request Smuggling (CWE-444)
description: Inconsistent parsing of Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding headers between the front-end proxy and back-end server allows request smuggling.
recommended_fix: Normalize on a single, RFC-compliant request-framing mechanism across the whole proxy chain, or disable HTTP/1.1 keep-alive to the back end.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (CWE-79)
description: User-controlled input from a query parameter is reflected into the HTML response without output encoding, allowing arbitrary script execution in a victim's browser.
recommended_fix: Apply context-aware output encoding at every reflection point and adopt a strict Content-Security-Policy as defense in depth.

title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) (CWE-639)
description: An object identifier in the URL/request body is used to fetch a resource with no ownership check, allowing access to another user's data by changing the ID.
recommended_fix: Enforce object-level authorization checks server-side on every request, not just at the UI layer.

title: Missing HTTP Security Headers (CWE-693)
description: The application does not send X-Frame-Options/Content-Security-Policy headers, leaving it vulnerable to clickjacking and reducing defense-in-depth against XSS.
recommended_fix: Add X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and a baseline Content-Security-Policy.

title: JWT Signature Verification Bypass ('alg: none') (CWE-290)

recommended_fix: Normalize on a single, RFC-compliant request-framing mechanism across the whole proxy chain, or disable HTTP/1.1 keep-alive to the back end.

title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection (CWE-611)
description: The XML parser resolves external entities in user-supplied XML, allowing local file disclosure or SSRF via a crafted DOCTYPE declaration.
recommended_fix: Disable external entity resolution and DTD processing in the XML parser configuration.

title: Open Redirect (CWE-601)
description: A redirect parameter accepts an arbitrary external URL without validation, enabling phishing links that appear to originate from a trusted domain.
recommended_fix: Validate redirect targets against an allowlist of relative paths or known internal hosts only.

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) (CWE-352)
description: A state-changing request has no anti-CSRF token and is accepted with only a session cookie, allowing a forged cross-site request to perform the action on a victim's behalf.
recommended_fix: Require a per-session anti-CSRF token on all state-changing requests and set the session cookie's SameSite attribute to Strict or Lax.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (CWE-79)
description: User-controlled input from a query parameter is reflected into the HTML response without output encoding, allowing arbitrary script execution in a victim's browser.
recommended_fix: Apply context-aware output encoding at every reflection point and adopt a strict Content-Security-Policy as defense in depth.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (CWE-79)

title: Session Cookie Missing 'HttpOnly' Attribute (CWE-1004)
description: The session cookie is accessible to client-side JavaScript, making it a direct target for theft via any XSS on the same origin.
recommended_fix: Set the HttpOnly attribute on all session/authentication cookies.

title: Directory Listing Enabled (CWE-200)
description: Directory browsing is enabled on a web-accessible path, exposing the full file listing of an application or asset directory.
recommended_fix: Disable directory listing in the web server configuration for all web-accessible paths.

title: Unrestricted File Upload (CWE-434)
description: The file upload feature does not validate file type/content, allowing a script file to be uploaded and potentially executed by the web server.
recommended_fix: Validate uploaded file content (not just extension), store uploads outside the web root, and disable script execution in the upload directory.

title: Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoint (CWE-307)
description: The login endpoint accepts unlimited authentication attempts from a single source with no throttling or lockout.
recommended_fix: Add per-account and per-IP rate limiting with exponential backoff on the authentication endpoint.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) (CWE-918)
description: A server-side fetch of a user-supplied URL is not restricted to an allowlist, allowing requests to internal-only services and cloud metadata endpoints.
recommended_fix: Validate/allowlist destination hosts for any server-initiated fetch, and block requests to link-local/metadata address ranges.

title: The vulnerability affects Ignition SCADA applications where Python scripting is utilized for automation purposes. The…
description:
The vulnerability affects Ignition SCADA applications where Python 
scripting is utilized for automation purposes. The vulnerability arises 
from the absence of proper security controls that restrict which Python 
libraries can be imported and executed within the scripting environment.
 The core issue lies in the Ignition service account having system 
permissions beyond what an Ignition privileged user requires. When an 
authenticated administrator uploads a malicious project file containing 
Python scripts with bind shell capabilities, the application executes 
these scripts with the same privileges as the Ignition Gateway process, 
which typically runs with SYSTEM-level permissions on Windows. 
Alternative code execution patterns could lead to similar results.
recommended_fix: Apply the vendor's security update for the affected firmware/software version, or isolate the device on a segmented network/VLAN if no patch is currently available.

title: Recently it was discovered as a part of the research on IoT devices in the most recent firmware for Shekar Endoscope…
description: Recently it was discovered as a part of the research on IoT devices in the most recent firmware for Shekar Endoscope that an attacker connected to the device Wi-Fi SSID can exploit a memory corruption issue and execute remote code on the device. This device acts as an Endoscope camera that allows its users to use it in various industrial systems and settings, car garages, and also in some cases in the medical clinics to get access to areas that are difficult for a human being to reach. Any breach of this system can allow an attacker to get access to video feed and pictures viewed by that user and might allow them to get a foot hold in air gapped networks especially in case of nation critical infrastructure/industries. The firmware contains binary uvc_stream that is the UDP daemon which is responsible for handling all the UDP requests that the device receives. The client application sends a UDP request to change the Wi-Fi name which contains the following format: "SETCMD0001+0001+[2 byte length of wifiname]+[Wifiname]. This request is handled by "control_Dev_thread" function which at address "0x00409AE0" compares the incoming request and determines if the 10th byte is 01 and if it is then it redirects to 0x0040A74C which calls the function "setwifiname". The function "setwifiname" uses a memcpy function but uses the length of the payload obtained by using strlen function as the third parameter which is the number of bytes to copy and this allows an attacker to overflow the function and control the $PC value.
recommended_fix: Apply the vendor's security update for the affected firmware/software version, or isolate the device on a segmented network/VLAN if no patch is currently available.

title: Visual Components (owned by KUKA) is a robotic simulator that allows simulating factories and robots in order…
description: Visual Components (owned by KUKA) is a robotic simulator that allows simulating factories and robots in order toimprove planning and decision-making processes. Visual Components software requires a special license which can beobtained from a network license server. The network license server binds to all interfaces (0.0.0.0) and listensfor packets over UDP port 5093. No authentication/authorization is required in order to communicate with theserver. The protocol being used is a property protocol by RMS Sentinel which provides the licensing infrastructurefor the network license server. RMS Sentinel license manager service exposes UDP port 5093 which provides sensitivesystem information that could be leveraged for further exploitation without any kind of authentication. Thisinformation includes detailed hardware and OS characteristics.After a decryption process, a textual protocol is found which contains a simple header with the requested command,application-identifier, and some arguments. The protocol leaks information regarding the receiving serverinformation, license information and managing licenses, among others.Through this flaw, attackers can retreive information about a KUKA simulation system, particularly, the version ofthe licensing server, which is connected to the simulator, and which will allow them to launch local simulationswith similar characteristics, further understanding the dynamics of motion virtualization and opening doors toother attacks (see RVDP#711 and RVDP#712 for subsequent vulnerabilities that compromise integrity andavailability).Beyond compromising simulations, Visual Components provides capabilities to interface with industrial machinery.Particularly, their PLC Connectivity feature 'makes it easy' to connect simulations with control systems usingeither the industry standard OPC UA or other supported vendor specific interfaces. This fills the gap of jumpingfrom simulation to real and enables attackers to pivot from the Visual Components simulator to robots or otherIndustrial Control System (ICS) devices, such as PLCs.
recommended_fix: Apply the vendor's security update for the affected firmware/software version, or isolate the device on a segmented network/VLAN if no patch is currently available.

title: A vulnerability in the TCP throttling process for Cisco IoT Field Network Director (IoT-FND) could allow an…
description: A vulnerability in the TCP throttling process for Cisco IoT Field Network Director (IoT-FND) could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the system to consume additional memory, eventually forcing the device to restart, aka Memory Exhaustion. The vulnerability is due to insufficient rate-limiting protection. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a high rate of TCP packets to a specific group of open listening ports on a targeted device. An exploit could allow the attacker to cause the system to consume additional memory. If enough available memory is consumed, the system will restart, creating a temporary denial of service (DoS) condition. The DoS condition will end after the device has finished the restart process. This vulnerability affects the following Cisco products: Connected Grid Network Management System, if running a software release prior to IoT-FND Release 4.0; IoT Field Network Director, if running a software release prior to IoT-FND Release 4.0. Cisco Bug IDs: CSCvc77164.

title: Recently it was discovered as a part of the research on IoT devices in the most recent firmware for Shekar Endoscope…
description: Recently it was discovered as a part of the research on IoT devices in the most recent firmware for Shekar Endoscope that the desktop application used to connect to the device suffers from a stack overflow if more than 26 characters are passed to it as the Wi-Fi name. This application is installed on the device and an attacker who can provide the right payload can execute code on the user's system directly. Any breach of this system can allow an attacker to get access to all the data that the user has access too. The application uses a dynamic link library(DLL) called "avilib.dll" which is used by the application to send binary packets to the device that allow to control the device. One such action that the DLL provides is change password in the function "sendchangename" which allows a user to change the Wi-Fi name on the device. This function calls a sub function "sub_75876EA0" at address 0x758784F8. The function determines which action to execute based on the parameters sent to it. The "sendchangename" passes the datastring as the second argument which is the name we enter in the textbox and integer 1 as first argument. The rest of the 3 arguments are set to 0. The function "sub_75876EA0" at address 0x75876F19 uses the first argument received and to determine which block to jump to. Since the argument passed is 1, it jumps to 0x75876F20 and proceeds from there to address 0x75876F56 which calculates the length of the data string passed as the first parameter. This length and the first argument are then passed to the address 0x75877001 which calls the memmove function which uses a stack address as the destination where the password typed by us is passed as the source and length calculated above is passed as the number of bytes to copy which leads to a stack overflow.
recommended_fix: Apply the vendor's security update for the affected firmware/software version, or isolate the device on a segmented network/VLAN if no patch is currently available.
